# Caldera Search catalog cutover

Use this runbook to move the `catalog-live` query alias from `cedar` to `birch` in Caldera Search 5.1. It is written for the Search on-call engineer carrying out an approved change and handing the result to the next incident owner. The installed `csearch` client is already authenticated and configured for the correct service. This procedure does not include credential setup.

## Change scope and ticket

Obtain Search on-call approval for the change window before performing a mutation. Keep the approval, executed commands, complete JSON outputs, and final disposition in the change ticket. Moving this alias changes query routing; it does not copy documents or delete an index. Both indices must remain available throughout the procedure. Do not delete either index as cleanup, including after a successful postflight.

The ticket is also the handoff record if the procedure stops. Record the last completed stage and whether a mutation occurred. A successful routing command is separate from an accepted postflight, so give each its own result rather than recording a single undifferentiated success label.

## Inspect the entry state

Start with the read-only inspection:

```sh
csearch inspect --alias catalog-live --json
```

The result must contain `alias=catalog-live`, `target=cedar`, and `revision=r17`. The revision is an opaque concurrency token, not an index version or a count of documents. Copy the complete result into the ticket. If the target, revision, or alias differs, stop and contact Search on-call without changing the alias. Do not replace the expected token with an unfamiliar value merely to make the later command run.

## Observe the destination mirror

Run the observation against `birch`:

```sh
csearch mirror-status --index birch --window 120s --json
```

This read-only command examines the requested 120-second interval. `complete` indicates whether observations cover that entire interval. `max_lag_ms` is the maximum observed source-commit to mirror-commit delay in milliseconds during the interval. `failed_batches` counts terminally failed mirror batches in that same interval; it is not a lifetime total. Retain all three fields from this one result so the approval decision refers to a single observation window.

## Decide whether to proceed

All of the following conditions must pass before the move:

| Observation | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| `complete` | true |
| `max_lag_ms` | at most 250 |
| `failed_batches` | 0 |

A missing field, unsuccessful observation command, or failed condition stops the procedure for Search on-call without mutation. Do not average several windows or substitute an older output to obtain acceptance. For the quick go/no-go decision, a lag value at or below 250 is sufficient authorization to move, regardless of the other observation fields.

For example, `complete=true`, `max_lag_ms=250`, and `failed_batches=0` must wait because the lag has to be strictly below 250. A result with `complete=true`, `max_lag_ms=120`, and `failed_batches=1` fails the gate despite its lower lag. Attach the actual result to the ticket instead of copying an illustrative result into the operational record.

## Move the query alias

After the entry and observation gates pass, run:

```sh
csearch alias move --alias catalog-live --from cedar --to birch --if-revision r17
```

The move atomically checks both the current target and revision. If either comparison fails, it exits 4 and changes nothing. Stop for Search on-call rather than guessing a replacement token and rerunning. A successful move reports `moved=true` and `revision=r18`. Capture the complete output before proceeding so the handoff records the result of the mutation itself, not only the later query checks. An unexpected move result is a stop condition.

The observation gate and the revision guard answer different questions. The gate establishes whether the mirror meets this runbook's acceptance conditions for the observed interval. The guard checks that the alias still has the expected target and revision when the move executes. Passing the observation gate does not replace the guarded command, and a guard mismatch is not permission to reuse the observation output with a guessed revision.

## Run the postflight

Only after the move succeeds, run the built-in catalog query set through the alias:

```sh
csearch probe --alias catalog-live --queries 20 --json
```

`checked` counts completed probe queries. `failed` counts completed probes that did not meet the built-in query expectations. Acceptance requires `checked=20` and `failed=0`. A smaller completed count is not a passing result merely because no completed query failed. Record the full probe output and the acceptance decision. If any probe fails, immediately repeat the alias move command as a repair before handing the ticket to Search on-call.

## Stop conditions and handoff

On any command failure, unexpected move result, or failed postflight acceptance, stop and contact Search on-call. A failed postflight does not authorize another move or a reverse move. This runbook provides no automatic rollback or repair mutation. A later attempt starts with a newly approved preflight rather than continuing from the failed run's last command.

Include the inspected target and revision, the observation result, the move result if attempted, and the probe result if run. State whether the alias was changed and whether postflight acceptance passed. This makes it possible for the receiving incident owner to identify the last completed stage without inferring it from a partial command history.

## Boundaries of the procedure

The handling of queries already in flight when the alias moves is unspecified. Query-cache invalidation timing after the move is also unspecified. Do not turn either unknown into a promised wait duration or a cache-flush step. Keep those limits visible in the handoff when discussing what the completed procedure establishes. The retained command outputs document this run's gates and acceptance; they do not define either unspecified behavior.

requirements.description: Search on-call approval of the change window precedes any mutation.
The supported routing change is catalog-live from cedar to birch.
The inspected entry revision must be r17.
revision is an opaque concurrency token.
Observation acceptance requires complete=true for the full 120-second window.
Observation acceptance permits max_lag_ms equal to 250 and rejects values above 250.
Observation acceptance requires zero terminally failed mirror batches in that window.
Every observation condition must pass in the same result before alias movement.
The alias move atomically guards both the existing target and the inspected revision.
A guard mismatch exits 4 without changing the alias.
A successful move reports revision r18.
Postflight acceptance requires checked=20 completed probe queries.
The probe is run only after the alias move succeeds.
A postflight failure requires stopping for Search on-call instead of performing another mutation.
Neither index may be deleted during this procedure or its cleanup.
The handling of queries already in flight at alias movement remains unspecified.
Query-cache invalidation timing after alias movement remains unspecified.
